import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Work from the frozen clean splits/objects where possible
full = df.drop(columns="_row_id") if "_row_id" in df.columns else df.copy()
TARGET = "Survived"
FEATURES = [c for c in full.columns if c != TARGET]

print("="*70)
print("A) DUPLICATE ROWS")
print("="*70)
dup_all = full.duplicated().sum()
dup_feat = full.duplicated(subset=FEATURES).sum()
dup_feat_label = full.duplicated(subset=FEATURES + [TARGET]).sum()
print(f"Exact duplicate rows (full row)          : {dup_all}")
print(f"Duplicate feature vectors (ignoring label): {dup_feat}")
print(f"Duplicate feature+label rows             : {dup_feat_label}")
if dup_feat > 0:
    print("\nDuplicate feature groups:")
    print(full[full.duplicated(subset=FEATURES, keep=False)]
          .sort_values(FEATURES))

print("\n" + "="*70)
print("B) LABEL LEAKAGE SCREEN")
print("="*70)
y = full[TARGET]
for c in full.columns:
    if c == TARGET:
        continue
    if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(full[c]):
        # correlation with target (|r|) — high values are suspicious
        r = full[c].corr(y)
        print(f"{c:<10} numeric  | corr_with_target = {r:+.3f}")
    else:
        # does each category perfectly determine the label?
        ct = pd.crosstab(full[c], y)
        # purity: max share of the majority label per category
        purity = (ct.div(ct.sum(axis=1), axis=0).max(axis=1))
        print(f"{c:<10} category | crosstab:\n{ct}\n"
              f"{'':<10}           per-category label purity={purity.round(2).to_dict()}")

# Any column that is constant -> zero information
print("\nConstant (zero-variance) columns:",
      [c for c in full.columns if full[c].nunique(dropna=False) <= 1])

# Near-unique identifier-like columns (n unique == n rows) -> leakage risk
print("Identifier-like columns (nunique == n_rows):",
      [c for c in full.columns if full[c].nunique(dropna=False) == len(full)])

print("\n" + "="*70)
print("C) AVAILABILITY AT PREDICTION TIME")
print("="*70)
# Heuristic: columns that describe post-outcome info or are identifiers
notes = {
  "Pclass":   "Ticket class — known at booking/prediction time. OK.",
  "Sex":      "Passenger attribute — known at prediction time. OK.",
  "Age":      "Passenger attribute — known at prediction time. OK.",
  "SibSp":    "Family info — known at prediction time. OK.",
  "Parch":    "Family info — known at prediction time. OK.",
  "Fare":     "Ticket price — known at booking. OK.",
  "Embarked": "Embarkation port — known at prediction time. OK.",
  "Survived": "TARGET — must never be used as a feature.",
}
for c in full.columns:
    print(f"{c:<10}: {notes.get(c, 'Review manually.')}")

print("\nFeature dtype summary:")
print(full[FEATURES].dtypes)
